editorial.headline: Audio and Video Retail Is Nationally Open—But Not for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This specialised retail activity spans audio, video and recording equipment, open nationally across every business scale but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, this activity cannot be registered as PMA in Bali today. That is the decisive local fact for a business centred on the island, even though the national position is open and permits foreign ownership up to 100%. The contrast is not a technical footnote: nationally open retail scope does not override Bali’s permanent, island-wide block on PMA registrations for activities classified as Low or Medium-Low risk.

The activity is specialised retail trade in audio and video equipment. Its scope includes radios, televisions, video equipment, tape recorders, audio amplifiers and cassette recorders, alongside stereo equipment, recordable media, and equipment for recording and playing CDs and DVDs. In practical terms, it describes a retail business built around the sale of dedicated sound, image and playback equipment rather than a general retail category. The record’s breadth matters: it reaches both the equipment itself and the media and devices used to record or play it.

At the national level, the activity is open to businesses at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. It is also nationally open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For an investor considering the national framework alone, that is a clear position: this activity may be structured with full foreign ownership. The applicable source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali changes the result for PMA registration. At the Large scale, the OSS risk assessment is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, placing the activity within Bali’s moratorium. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. So the national 100% ceiling remains the national ceiling, but it does not make a PMA registration available in Bali. For founders, the responsible reading is straightforward: the business activity is nationally foreign-open across all listed scales, while Bali currently blocks its PMA registration because of the recorded risk classification and moratorium.
